text.p: - Swiss Federal Police Agency reported that crime in 1996 registered an upward trend for the first time since 1992. Police seized significantly larger quantities of illegal drugs -- especially so-called designer drugs such as ecstasy -- than the year before.

- Swiss state-owned telecommunication agency Telecom PTT will operate under the name of Swisscom as from October 1997 in run-up to liberalisatuion and parial privatisation from 1998. - Swiss pharmaceuticals giant Roche reported a 16 percent rise in 1996 net profits to 3.9 billion Swiss francs. Sales reached 15.96 billion francs, up 11 percent compared with the previous

- The Swiss federation of chocolate producers criticized legal limbo over the status of genetically-altered soy products after 500 tons of chocolate had to be recalled for containing lecithin made from gene soja. The modified soja has been approved fro use in Europe but Swiss approval has been held up by a legal challenge from environmental groups.
- Swiss raw materials group Suedelektra reported a 1996 net profit of $44.4 million, down from $75.9 million the previous year.

- Some 130 regional public employment offices set up to help the unemployed to find jobs have been flooded by job seekers. Some 650 additional jobs need to be created to meet the demand. - Swiss biologists announced a 'manifesto for human dignity', which supports a constitutional ban on cloning human beings but not on animal cloning.
